1. The Marshall House - Savannah, Georgia

Savannah has long been known for its thriving ghost population, many of whom have taken up residence at the city’s oldest hotel. Established in 1851 by Mary Magdalene Marshall, the building has played many roles: a makeshift hospital during the mid-19th-century yellow fever epidemic, a Union hospital near the end of the Civil War, and a temporary home to Joel Chandler Harris, creator of Uncle Remus, during the Reconstruction era. It’s no wonder then that guests frequently report odd activity in the hotel’s period-detailed rooms and cozy library. Common occurrences include the sound of children running down the halls at night, strange figures spotted in the foyers, doorknobs rattling, and faucets turning on on their own. Many Savannah ghost tours stop outside the hotel, but nothing beats drinking spirits amongst the spirits during the nightly social hour (sometimes with live entertainment!).

2. The 1886 Crescent Hotel and Spa - Eureka Springs, Arkansas

For a long time, the Crescent Hotel seemed cursed: Just before it opened, in 1886, a stonemason working on the structure fell to his death and later, in the early 20th-century, a young woman may or may not have been pushed out of a top floor window. Eventually, the hotel landed in the hands of Norman Baker, a quack doctor who “treated” his mental patients using inhumane methods. (He was eventually arrested but only after plenty of damage was already done.) Needless to say, there are numerous rumors that now swirl around the hotel, with many visitors spotting doctors, nurses, and patients from the hospital roaming the corridors. Room 218, where the stonemason met his end, is considered the most haunted spot in the hotel, but most anywhere you venture you’ll find mysteries galore. The staff leads daily ghost tours — including a look at Baker’s old autopsy table in the basement — and there are even midnight ESP investigations for especially fearless guests.

3. The Drovers Inn - Argyll and Bute, Scotland

This rural Scottish inn on the edge of Loch Lomond is home to a colorful cast of spirits, including an entire family. Legend has it that this family got lost in the snow while looking for shelter, all of them freezing to death in the night. Now, in death, they’ve finally gotten their wish of a place to stay in room two at the inn. Meanwhile, down the hall in room six lives a little girl who supposedly drowned in the river behind the building. Guests staying in her room have, on occasion, seen her small figure dripping in water and have even felt her in the bed beside them. Last but not least, there’s Angus: a young cattle drover who was murdered by members of a rival clan and now screams in pain as he wanders the property for eternity. After you’ve greeted the ghosts, make sure to grab a pint from the inn’s bar and restaurant, where taxidermy animals, old china dishes, and exposed wooden beams transport you back in time. The most daring guests of all will not shy away from a heaping plate of haggis or a hefty helping of mince and tatties.

4. Hotel Alex Johnson - Rapid City, South Dakota

Railroad tycoon Alex Johnson built this hotel in 1927 to attract high society to Mount Rushmore, the West’s newest tourist trap. Though he passed away in 1938, his dream came true: Over the years, the hotel hosted six U.S. presidents and even served as a temporary home for Alfred Hitchcock and Cary Grant during the filming of “North by Northwest.” It’s a testament to the grandeur of Hotel Alex Johnson that none of its famous guests were deterred by its more mysterious elements, i.e., the Lady in White who haunts the eighth floor. This bride supposedly jumped to her death while staying at the hotel on her wedding night, and now, guests wake up to her opening their windows and dresser drawers. If you don’t see the Lady in White, you might instead spot John himself, who still keeps an eye on day-to-day business with his young daughter by his side. For amateur ghost hunters, the hotel offers a ghost adventure package that includes lodging in a haunted room, a ghost detector, and other, less-haunted perks like a $25 dining credit and free valet parking.

5. The Lodge at Hot Lake Springs - La Grande, Oregon

Everything was going swimmingly for this hot springs resort until, in 1934, a raging fire destroyed half the building and put it out of business. In the years after, the space was used as a nurse’s training school, a retirement home, a restaurant, and an insane asylum; however, in 1991, it was entirely abandoned and left to the elements. During this 15-year offseason, many a story started to spread about The Lodge, such as it being haunted by (among others) a gardener who committed suicide on the property, a nurse who perished in the lake, and a number of asylum inmates. So dark did this once-grand establishment’s reputation become that it appeared on the ABC series “The Scariest Places on Earth” in 2001. Two years later, new owners cleaned up the building and reopened it to the public as a spa and B&B with geothermal soaking pools, a bar and restaurant, and a 60-seat movie theater. The Lodge is a bit reticent to discuss its dicey past, but guests still report odd figures in windows, random screams, and a piano playing itself.


6. Gran Hotel Bolivar - Lima, Peru

In its heyday, Gran Hotel Bolivar was the swankiest place to stay in all of Lima, welcoming politicians, artists, Hollywood stars, and rock legends. The Rolling Stones spent the night here (before being kicked out for poor behavior), while Ava Gardner once danced barefoot in the bar. Charles de Gaulle, Orson Welles, and Ernest Hemingway are just a few of the hotel’s many other renowned guests. However, by the time it was declared a national landmark in 1972, Gran Hotel was on the decline; new, modern hotels pulled away business and its sketchy owner fled the country, leaving financial ruin in his wake. It was around this same time that ghost stories started to emerge, with “insiders” claiming that the hotel’s fifth and sixth floors were closed not (as reported) for financial reasons but because they were severely haunted by former guests and employees. Even on the floors that are still operational, ghosts have been said to turn on and off the coffeemakers, radios, and televisions.

7. St. James Hotel - Cimarron, New Mexico

Back in the day, as Americans journeyed out west, this hotel offered weary travelers a place to rest their heads (and get a cold drink). Many outlaws like Wyatt Earp, Jesse James, Billy the Kid, and Buffalo Bill Cody stopped here on their way down the Santa Fe Trail, and thus (unsurprisingly), the inn became known for its frequent murders. (Supposedly, “Wonder who got killed at Lambert’s place this weekend?” was a common question around Cimarron.) With the exception of a modern annex, the hotel still looks much like it did in the days when drinking, gambling, and guns were the norm, with a creaky wooden staircase, deer antlers on the walls, and a big stone fireplace in the dining room. There’s only one bedroom that guests are unable to book: room 18, where T.J. Wright, infamous ne’er-do-well and onetime owner of the hotel, was killed by an unknown gunman. Doomed to the room for eternity, he does not take too kindly to visitors.

8. The Mermaid Inn - Rye, England

With more than 600 years of history under its belt, it’s easy to see why this quaint inn is one of the world’s most haunted places to stay. Factor in that it was built shortly after French raiders burned all of Rye to the ground, and it’s no wonder there are some restless souls lingering around. The cellars beneath the inn date back all the way to the 12th century, and the secret tunnels connecting them were once used by smugglers from the notorious Hawkhurst Gang. In fact, many folks believe that members of the gang still use the tunnels today, even roaming upstairs to visit guests from time to time. The inn’s 31 rooms are all named after notable people from either Rye’s or the inn’s history, and a handful of them are also said to be haunted. Among the resident spirits are two 16th-century swordsmen, engaged in a perpetual duel in room 16, and the wife of gang leader Arthur Gray in room 17.

9. Hotel del Coronado - San Diego, California

The self-proclaimed “birthplace of the American beach vacation” has wowed big-time guests for over a century. Marilyn Monroe, Charlie Chaplin, President Franklin D. Roosevelt, and L. Frank Baum all enjoyed its luxury suites and sandy beaches, surely reveling in the relative privacy afforded on a tidal island. The hotel has many claims to fame, from lighting up the world’s first outdoor electric Christmas tree, to being featured in the film “Some Like it Hot,” to — you guessed it — housing a famous ghost. In 1892, 24-year-old Kate Morgan checked into the hotel and never checked out, her body found on an exterior staircase with a gunshot wound to the head (which the coroner ruled a suicide). If you tire of Hotel Del’s luxury and want a bit more spook in your stay, take a walk past Kate’s room, where many odd phenomena have been reported. Guests and staff alike have recalled sudden cold breezes, phantom footsteps, and electronics turning on and off on their own. Some have even spotted a Victorian woman dressed in black wandering the halls or standing alone down at the seashore.

10. Clown Motel - Tonopah, Nevada

This eerily jolly roadside fully embraces its role as nightmare fodder, leaning into the common fear of clowns with horror-movie-themed rooms (all with a clown twist, of course). From “Friday the 13th” to “Chucky” to “Halloween,” the motel lets you choose which creepy world you wish to enter. Even the “normal,” non-movie rooms are a bit disconcerting, with strange clown wall art and plenty of ghosts. The cemetery right next to the motel is home to such distinguished residents as Bina Verrault, a conwoman from New York; Sheriff Thomas Logan, who was shot while investigating a local brothel; and Clarence David, the father of motel co-founders Leroy and Leona David. In fact, Clarence’s 150 clown statues formed the first of the Clown Motel’s collection, which has since expanded to over 4,000 pieces of clown memorabilia. In a 2015 episode of “Ghost Adventures,” host Zak Bagans and his crew explored the motel’s spiritual resonances and even captured on camera the hand of a large clown moving entirely of its own accord.

11. The Mizpah Hotel - Tonopah, Nevada

Just down the road from the Clown Motel, the Mizpah offers a completely different (but equally spooky) experience. Built in 1907, at the height of Tonopah’s silver boom, the hotel was long a hub for investors visiting from the east coast; however, as silver prospects slowly declined, the Mizpah floundered and ultimately closed its doors in 2000. After sitting abandoned for 11 years, it was purchased by the owners of several Sonoma wineries and restored to its former glory — a process that included capitalizing on its many spooky stories. Among the hotel’s undead residents are U.S. Senator Key Pittman (whose body was hidden in a bathtub full of ice within his suite) and the Lady in Red, a 1920s prostitute who was strangled by one of her clients on the fifth floor. At the front check-in desk, guests are encouraged to write about their encounters with the Lady in Red (or any of the other ghosts) in a dedicated notebook; some have even left photos of their supernatural experiences.

12. The Stanley Hotel - Estes Park, Colorado

It was after a stay here, in room 217, that Stephen King dreamed up his 1977 horror masterpiece, “The Shining,” shaping the fictional Overlook Hotel in the mold of this mountainside retreat. In fact, early in the novel, room 217 is mentioned as a place that the clairvoyant son, Danny, must avoid under all circumstances. However, the Stanley was home to eerie activity long before King made it famous, with the story going that its founder, Freelan O. Stanley, still drifts through the lobby and billiards room from time to time. Guests have also heard children running and playing at odd hours, witnessed cupboard doors unlock and open on their own, and, in room 407, spotted a cowboy apparition (perhaps the spirit of local legend “Rocky Mountain Jim.”) The Stanley proudly embraces its haunted reputation: playing the 1980 film adaptation of “The Shining” on an endless loop on the hotel TVs and leading a number of different ghost tours all year long. There’s the classic Stanley ghost tour, a “Shining” tour, a seasonal Halloween tour, and even a one-of-a-kind Frozen Dead Guy tour (which is basically exactly what it sounds like).

Leigh Myers’ signature cookies are crispy on the edges, tender in the center, and jazzed up with spicy nuts.

Ingredients


1 1/2 cup (200 grams) all-purpose flour


1 teaspoon baking soda


1 teaspoon fine sea salt


1 teaspoon cinnamon


16 tablespoons (228 grams) unsalted butter, softened


1 cup (188 grams) packed brown sugar


1/2 cup (118 grams) granulated sugar


2 large eggs, at room temperature


4 tablespoons heavy cream


4 teaspoons pure vanilla extract


3 cups (216 grams) old-fashioned rolled oats


2 cups (278 grams) semi-sweet chocolate chips


1 cup (126 grams) cayenne-pepper-toasted, chopped pecans**

**toast pecans:
 1 cup chopped pecans,
 1 teaspoon ground cayenne, 1 tablespoon melted butter

 

Directions

Step 1. Preheat oven to 350 F. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper. Toss the
pecans, cayenne, and butter together. Spread out on the baking sheet and bake for 10
minutes. Let the nuts cool before using.


Step 2. Keep oven at 350 and line cookie sheets with parchment paper.


Step 3. Whisk the flour, baking soda, salt, and cinnamon in a small bowl. Whisk it good.
Mix the butter and both sugars in a large bowl with a wooden spoon until it’s creamy
and screaming for mercy. Beat in the egg until incorporated, then stir in the cream and
vanilla.


Step 4. Add the flour mixture and gently stir until no traces of flour remain. Add the
oats, chocolate chips and nuts, folding them in until evenly distributed. Loosely scoop a
rounded ball of dough - I use a 2 tbsp ice cream scoop - and drop onto prepared sheet,
spacing your balls 2 inches apart.


Step 5. Bake, 1 sheet at a time, until golden brown, 12 to 14 minutes. Cool on the sheet
for 1 minute, then transfer cookies to wire rack to cool completely.

Though Cincinnati is best known for breweries, another effervescent beverage has a long history in the Queen City: the nectar soda.

Home to the oldest pharmacy college in the U.S. west of the Alleghenies, the Eclectic Medical Institute (1845-1952), and Lloyd Brothers Pharmacists, Cincinnati was long on the forefront of the pharmaceutical industry. The city had a number of apothecaries with soda fountains, as well as confectioners serving countless carbonated concoctions—some claiming to cure a variety of ailments, and others simply providing customers with something sweet and refreshing to drink.

Enter the nectar soda. The flavor is a combination of vanilla and bitter almond, and the drink is pastel pink in color—a nod to the hue of almond flowers, according to Dann Woellert, a Cincinnati food historian, etymologist, and the author of Cincinnati Candy: A Sweet History. Nicknamed the “drink of the gods,” the bitter almond flavor of nectar soda balances out what would otherwise be overly sweet vanilla, creating an addictive taste that grows on you with each sip. 

Nectar sodas have been served in Cincinnati since at least the late 1870s, though, like many iconic foods and beverages, its precise origins are murky. The only other U.S. city to embrace nectar sodas was New Orleans, but unlike Cincinnati, the tradition fizzled out in the Big Easy in the mid-20th century. Plus, Woellert says that the Queen City popularized them first. “They were served in Cincinnati nearly a decade before New Orleans,” he says.

While the Cincinnati nectar soda has multiple origin stories, each crediting a different pharmacist or confectioner, Woellert has concluded that John Mullane created the flavor after traveling to Quebec City to learn the art of confectionery from a prominent Canadian candymaker. He began serving nectar sodas in his confectionery shop in downtown Cincinnati in the late 1870s.

So, why did the nectar soda end up in Cincinnati and New Orleans, of all places? Wollert suspects that the bitter almond and vanilla flavor was used by the French Acadians who settled in both Quebec City and New Orleans.

Though nectar sodas aren’t as common as they were in the early 20th century, when they could be found at countless confectioneries and pharmacy soda fountains across Cincinnati, they’re still served at establishments throughout the city and the surrounding area. Nectar sodas have been on the menu at ice cream and chocolate shop Aglamesis Brothers since it opened in Cincinnati in 1908, if not shortly thereafter. That’s according to company president and CEO Randy Young, who is also a third-generation family member. 

It’s unclear when nectar sodas were added to the menu at Graeter’s, a Cincinnati ice cream and chocolate shop that opened in 1870 and now has locations throughout the city and the Midwest, but Chip Graeter, chief of retail operations and a fourth-generation family member, says that they were especially popular throughout the 1940s, 1950s and 1960s.

In a January 28, 1947 article in the Cincinnati Enquirer, Tom Moore, the head of the soda department at Dow Drug Store—which operated 32 soda fountains throughout the metropolitan area at that time—said that “nectar is one of the most popular flavors in all of their stores, and has been for many years.” Five years prior, Dow ran an ad in the same newspaper which read: “Be glad you live in Cincinnati, the only place in the country where you can enjoy a Dow double-dip nectar soda.”

Originally, nectar syrup was made by combining half-and-half or milk with water, bitter almond extract, vanilla extract and red food coloring. While Aglamesis eventually switched to a dairy-free shelf-stable syrup, Graeter's recipe has never changed—it still contains milk and needs to be refrigerated. 

Both Aglamesis and Graeter’s make nectar soda by mixing nectar syrup with a dollop of whipped cream, adding a scoop or two of vanilla ice cream, then topping it off with some soda water and more whipped cream.

Though Young says that nectar sodas are most popular with older adults, they’re also a hit with members of younger generations who try them. “People who grew up with them still love them today,” Graeter says. “We still make them in all of our stores, but they're not nearly as popular today as they once were, simply because milkshakes and smoothies have taken over.”  

According to Young, there is a commercially available descendant of the nectar soda. “Commercial soda companies like Barqs and others came out with their version of cream soda—a bright pink soda—which got its flavoring from nectar soda,” he explains.

items.title: Alta Rock Carvings in Alta, Norway
items.summary: One of the most extraordinary attractions in northern Norway is Alta Museum's outdoor area, where thousands of prehistoric carvings can be found. These are not paintings or replicas displayed behind glass – they are original artworks carved directly into the bedrock by people thousands of years ago. Some of the carvings date back more than 7,000 years, making them among the oldest and most significant examples of prehistoric rock art in Northern Europe. They depict reindeer, bears, elk, fish, whales, boats, hunting scenes, fishing activities, human figures and mysterious rituals. The carvings were originally made near the shoreline, and as the land gradually rose after the last Ice Age, new rock surfaces became available for successive generations of artists. items.title: Shrine of the Most Blessed Sacrement in Hanceville, Alabama
items.summary: Extraordinary architecture designed to resemble a 13th-century Italian Franciscan church, particularly the Basilica of Saint Francis of Assisi. Marble floors, gold ornamentation, stained glass, and soaring ceilings. The Spanish religious-art workshop Talleres de Arte Granda, founded in Madrid in 1891, designed and furnished the church's interior. It was founded by Mother Angelica, the founder of EWTN, and opened in 1999. Three donors provided all of the funds needed for construction and completion.

The collection rarely gets updated, and the once-popular TV stars are now unfamiliar to the younger audience. items.title: Promotions Gallery in Paris, France
items.summary: Historically, a secret entrance at the School of Mines, known as the “Mines staircase,” provided students access to the Paris Catacombs . Although this private access is no longer available for use due to safety reasons, the General Inspector of Quarries still grants students permission to uphold this artistic tradition. Each year, on the occasion of Sainte-Barbe, celebrated on December 4th in honor of the patron saint of miners, first-year students create a painting representing their class, continuing the tradition.

items.title: Čigoč Stork Village in Kratečko, Croatia
items.summary: In the Croatian village of Čigoč, some of the most conspicuous residents live above the rooftops. White storks build bulky nests on traditional wooden houses, sharing the settlement with the people below. Situated in Lonjsko Polje Nature Park beside the Tišina oxbow of the Sava River, the village is surrounded by wet meadows, pastures, and pools. These habitats provide feeding grounds close to the nests, allowing adult birds to gather frogs, insects, and other small animals for their young. In 1994, the conservation foundation EuroNatur named Čigoč the first European Stork Village. The designation recognised the village’s importance for white storks and its long-standing relationship between people, traditional farming, and wildlife. It also launched an initiative that would connect stork

items.title: Thunder Hole in Bar Harbor, Maine
items.summary: Located in Maine's Acadia National Park, along the rocky shoreline of Mount Desert Island, Thunder Hole is a natural geological formation known for producing a booming, thunder-like sound phenomenon that gives it its name, as well as for explosive water sprays reaching up to 40 feet. Resulting from glacial activity over thousands of years ago, what began as a small, natural fissure in the solid granite cliffs, slowly gave way to the 10 foot wide channel seen today. As high tide rolls in, and wave force increases, water rushes into this channel, and into a small underwater cavern contained therein. When an incoming wave forces water into this cavern, trapped air in the cavern is compressed and then escapes, almost as if through the blow hole of a whale, with magnificent water sprays and rev

items.title: Abdulla Avloni Memorial Museum in Tashkent, Uzbekistan
items.summary: Most memorial museums stay put in the house of the person they remember. This one moved out. It was founded in 1968 in the Tashkent house where Abdulla Avloni (1878–1934) had lived with his family from 1910 until his death. Avloni was one of the Jadids, the Muslim reformers who believed Central Asia could be renewed through new-method schools, newspapers and the theatre. He opened schools, wrote their textbooks, published the newspaper Shuhrat and, in 1913, gathered the Turon theatre troupe. In 1993 the museum left the house for the institute that carries Avloni's name, where teachers from all over Uzbekistan now come to brush up their skills. Without its original walls, it relies on things to bring him close: his desk, typewriter and candlestick, his bookcase and wardrobe, even his clothe

items.title: Podcast: Exploring Alberta’s Rich History in Fiction
items.summary: Listen and subscribe on Apple Podcasts , Spotify , and all major podcast apps. In this episode of The Atlas Obscura Podcast , we’re exploring the surprising side of Alberta with the Canadian novelist Esi Edugyan. Our podcast is an audio guide to the world’s wondrous, awe-inspiring, strange places. In under 15 minutes, we’ll take you to an incredible site, and along the way you’ll meet some fascinating people and hear their stories. Join us daily, Monday through Thursday, to explore a new wonder with host Kelly McEvers and guests. This is an edited transcript of the Atlas Obscura Podcast: a celebration of the world’s strange, incredible, and wondrous places. Find the show on Apple Podcasts, Spotify, and all major podcast apps. items.title: Binh Lam Champa Tower in Tuy Phước Đông, Vietnam
items.summary: Unlike most surviving Cham towers that crown dramatic hilltops, Binh Lam Tower rises almost unexpectedly from the flat, verdant plains of a quiet lowland village. Constructed around the late tenth to early eleventh century, this 20-meter brick sanctuary serves as a vital architectural bridge, catching the art form mid-evolution between the delicate, lyrical features of the My Son A1 style and the grand, spear-like forms of classic Binh Dinh towers. Its weathered facade features slender vertical pilasters, mini-temple false doors, and faint relief carvings of the mythical bird-god Garuda. Beyond its standing brickwork, Binh Lam hides deep subterranean secrets: archaeological digs uncovered vast foundations of a once-extensive religious complex, alongside stone Nagas and relief sculptures. items.title: National Underground Railroad Freedom Center in Cincinnati, Ohio
items.summary: The National Underground Railroad Freedom Center, located in Cincinnati along the banks of the Ohio River makes a solemn statement about the lives that were lived enslaved in the early history of the United States, and the many heroic men and women who played important roles in the Underground Railroad movement, which helped to bring an end to African slavery in the United States. Referred to as a "museum of conscience", The Freedom Center is dedicated to exploring the struggle to abolish human enslavement. During the era when the Underground Railroad was active, Cincinnati was a major gateway across the Ohio River where freedom seekers escaped from southern slave states to the northern states or Canada, making the Center's location rather significant. Having opened its doors in 2004, the

items.title: Veliki Kalnik Castle in Koprivnica, Croatia
items.summary: Above the village of Kalnik in northern Croatia, the walls of Veliki Kalnik Castle rise from a jagged rocky ridge. Built across several levels, the medieval stronghold follows the natural contours of the rock, making its surviving towers and walls appear to grow out of the mountain. First documented in 1243, the castle is best known for a story involving King Béla IV of Hungary and Croatia. According to local legend, the king took refuge here during the Mongol invasion of the 13th century. As the siege dragged on and supplies dwindled, villagers kept the defenders fed with plums. The grateful king is said to have rewarded his rescuers with noble status. They became known as the kalnički šljivari—the “plum nobles of Kalnik.” This tale remains part of the region’s identity, connecting an imp

items.title: The Crucified Tongkonan of Tolu Deri in North Toraja Regency, Indonesia
items.summary: In the highland villages of North Toraja, the skyline is dominated by tongkonan —traditional ancestral houses with sweeping, boat-shaped saddle roofs that loom dramatically over the landscape. For centuries, these wooden structures have served as the spiritual and social anchor for Torajan clans, decorated strictly according to Aluk Todolo ("the way of the ancestors"), the indigenous animist belief system. Their facades are traditionally adorned with carved geometric patterns ( pa'ssura' ), water buffalo horns ( kabongo' ), and sculpted wooden heads ( katik ) symbolizing wealth, status, and protection. However, in the small hamlet of Tolu Deri, just north of Rantepao, one particular tongkonan stands out as a striking, visually arresting symbol of modern Torajan syncretism. Mounted directly

Will Ferguson: If you drive east from Calgary, instead of going towards Banff and the mountains, if you go the other way, the landscape will suddenly fall away and you’ll find yourself in the Badlands. But before you hit that valley, before you make that descent, if you turn off the main road, you will come to a small hidden valley full of wild roses. In that little valley, you will find a small and improbable town—a town that should not exist. It's at the very edge of these rolling canola fields, roses, a little valley. items.summary: Our latest book, “America Obscura: An Explorer’s Guide to the Hidden Wonders of the United States,” has just been published. But it doesn’t just take you to Texas or Maine or Michigan. It takes you to a town called Hell, to a desert in one of the greenest states, to a sundial on the exact spot where America's day begins, and to a seven-story Jesus nicknamed “Our Milk Carton with Arms.” These are real places you can visit, and they are so dang unique. Since you’ll be driving, riding the rails or flying to reach a lot of them, we built you a soundtrack to match. Every song here is tied to a specific spot in the book . items.title: 8 Gargoyles and Grotesques Hiding in Plain Sight
items.summary: What’s more wondrous than towering spires on a building? Stained glass? Vaulted windows, or garden roofs? One word: Ghouls. Nothing jazzes up a normal old cathedral or mansion more than a mischievous face etched in stone, smiling (or, more likely, grimacing) at those passing below. Gargoyles and grotesques, in their own endearingly ugly way, are one of the best ways for architects to let their creations stand apart from the pack and inspire reflection for centuries to come. While most of these creatures are made in a similar style, with recognizable bodily features, expressions, and poses, there are a handful around the globe that are unapologetically unique: sometimes familiar, sometimes offbeat, and always worth a closer look. items.title: Only-in-Anchorage Winter Traditions
items.summary: Winter brings out the best of Anchorage . Under a blanket of snow, the city comes alive with festivals exploring regional history, lively tributes to Indigenous culture, decades-old sled dog races, and comfort food best enjoyed with friends and family. Here, Alaska’s adventurous spirit is felt in the traditions of diverse communities and seasonal occasions that offer a little something for everyone. Whether you’re taking in the shimmering colors of the aurora borealis from a snowmobile or enjoying films by up-and-coming artists at the Bear Tooth Theatrepub, there’s no shortage of events to make a winter in Anchorage one for the books. items.title: Anchorage: A City Within the Wild
items.summary: In Anchorage , exploring nature isn’t only for a rare free day or a well-planned vacation; it’s a part of daily life, as integral to the city as its infrastructure and cultural offerings. A day here may start with a morning walk on any of the hundreds of miles of trails, continue with freshly caught salmon for lunch at a restaurant with coastal views, and end with a sunset picnic on a rocky outcropping, where the only sounds are crashing waves and the fleeting glimpses of beluga whales. Located on a coastal plain that shifts into alpine slopes farther east, Anchorage is unique in how its different ecosystems overlap, creating rich diversity in wildlife, botany, and geology. You can experience the best of nature while still enjoying all the creature comforts of urban life and stumble across

items.title: Where to See the World’s Creepiest Dolls and Toys
items.summary: Humans have played with dolls for thousands of years, but it was not until the 18th century, when improved manufacturing rendered them more lifelike, that they started to be seen as sinister. Doll makers pivoted to porcelain skin, glass eyes, and wigs made of human hair, creating children and babies whose uncanniness to real people made them more unnerving than lovable. Later, in the Victorian Era, “mourning dolls” became a common way to remember deceased children, wearing their clothes and even sitting atop their coffins. Throw in Chucky, Annabelle, Slappy the Dummy, and numerous other evil dolls from pop culture, and boom: Dolls = creepy. At these places around the world, dolls and other eerie toys are the main attraction. Some spots are happy-go-lucky art projects that, despite their cr

items.title: Where to See the World’s Most Famous Preserved Body Parts
items.summary: Sure, you’ve seen a dead body before, but have you ever seen a thumb preserved in salt? How about a saint’s heart shrouded in gold? Beyond the normal displays of skeletons in medical museums and holy leaders’ bodies in churches and temples, there’s a whole world of bits and pieces to explore. Throughout history, body parts have been taken as trophies during wartime, worshipped as miraculous healing agents, cut off and displayed to honor their owners, or simply saved incidentally by natural processes. If seeing a whole body feels banal, we recommend delving from the complete corpse to its components. Here are some of our favorites from around the world. 1. items.title: Atlas Obscura’s Guide to America’s Most Haunted Cemeteries
items.summary: It’s nice to imagine death as an endless deep sleep, but not everyone is so lucky. In cemeteries across the U.S., you’ll find souls whose final resting places are not, in fact, restful at all. Perhaps they died with scores unsettled or, perhaps, their graves were ravaged by greedy developers. Sometimes, heartbreak rendered them unable to move on peacefully; in other cases, they simply couldn’t resist the chance to toy with their living visitors. One thing is certain: These restless spirits can turn otherwise serene sites into delightfully dark destinations, where the beauty of old headstones and manicured grounds is tinged with something indescribably eerie. When you gear up for your next cross-country road trip, let the energy of spooky season guide you to these cemeteries and graveyards

items.title: It All Comes Together in Chattanooga
items.summary: Chattanooga may be best known for its natural beauty, surrounded by mountains, valleys, and the Tennessee River. This charming Appalachian city is also home to annual music festivals like the IBMA World of Bluegrass and the 3 Sisters Bluegrass Festival . The streets and venues fill with musicians and fans dedicated to upholding the traditions of bluegrass music. Chattanooga has always been a city of convergence. Long before trains arrived, the river drew people through a narrow passage in the mountains; later came traders, artists, and entrepreneurs. At festival time, bluegrass becomes the city's soundtrack, with impromptu performances and jams ranging all across town. Many of the local hot spots are pressed into service as music venues. items.title: The Best Haunted Hotels to Book for a Spooky Getaway
items.summary: Nothing beats staying in a hotel whose suites hold some stories — especially if they’re of the spooky variety. The same friends who roll their eyes at mentions of luxury amenities and amazing views will be wide-eyed when you tell them about the ghost you accidentally ate breakfast with, the wailings you heard on your way to the icebox, or your run-in with an uncanny Victorian woman wearing all black. Booking a room at a regular old hotel will give you a few nice photos and a comfy robe; booking a room at a haunted one will give you tales of terror to tell for the rest of your life. At these hotels, lodges, inns, and resorts around the world, the supernatural is embraced and the unsettling is celebrated. items.summary: Joan Weed found this shortcake recipe on the back of a magazine and decided to make it her own. items.title: Nectar Soda
items.summary: Though Cincinnati is best known for breweries, another effervescent beverage has a long history in the Queen City: the nectar soda. Home to the oldest pharmacy college in the U.S. west of the Alleghenies, the Eclectic Medical Institute (1845-1952), and Lloyd Brothers Pharmacists , Cincinnati was long on the forefront of the pharmaceutical industry. The city had a number of apothecaries with soda fountains, as well as confectioners serving countless carbonated concoctions—some claiming to cure a variety of ailments, and others simply providing customers with something sweet and refreshing to drink. <item><title>28个品牌挤进电解质水行列，好自在逆势双位数增长：元气森林打的两场“硬仗”</title><link>https://www.chinanews.com.cn/cj/2026/11-21/10735701.shtml</link><description>
　　2026年的饮料行业，分化态势逐渐明显。据马上赢对全国典型门店的监测，2026年第二季度，汽水、即饮果汁、有糖即饮茶、包装水、能量饮料、运动饮料等品类几乎全线下滑，跌幅在8%至15%之间；大盘之中，仅无糖即饮茶保持16.1%的增长。</description>
<pubDate>Sat, 21 Nov 2026 13:40:09 +0800</pubDate>
</item>
<item><title>再创国内新纪录！中国石油新疆油田裸眼深部取换套试验取得重大突破</title><link>https://www.chinanews.com.cn/cj/2026/11-21/10735698.shtml</link><description>
　　中新网乌鲁木齐11月21日电 (孙亭文 刘尚红 高迎春)记者21日从中国石油新疆油田获悉，在新疆油田陆梁油田戈壁井场进行攻关的裸眼深部取换套扩大试验近日顺利收官，圆满完成1819米套管回接与环空固井作业，一举刷新国内深部裸眼取换套最长施工纪录，成为新疆油田套损套变治理技术体系迭代升级的又一标志性成果。</description>
<pubDate>Sat, 21 Nov 2026 13:36:49 +0800</pubDate>
</item>

items.summary: 11月15日，由中国青年企业家协会主办的2026年青年企业家创新发展大会在北京顺义召开。会议以“聚势新质生产力，赋能青年企业家”为主题，深入学习宣传贯彻党的二十届五中全会精神，引导青年企业家以创新发展服务经济社会高质量发展。

items.title: 产业规模破万亿元！高铁直达、夜场升级，冰雪消费提前升温
items.summary: 新一轮冰雪季开启，我国冰雪消费呈现出不少新变化：秋假带动亲子冰雪游提前升温，南方游客持续涌入北方雪场，冰雪产业规模突破万亿元。冰雪游正从季节性运动体验，向亲子研学、休闲度假和综合消费延伸，为冬季文旅市场注入新活力。

items.title: “三医”协同持续发力 天津北辰探索公立医院改革新路径
items.summary: 中新网天津11月21日电 (记者 江莹)20日，天津市北辰区举办“卫健护航见行见效”专题新闻发布会，介绍该区深化医疗、医保、医药“三医”协同发展治理、优化高水平诊疗供给、提升医院精细化管理相关进展。作为国家第二批公立医院综合改革示范区，北辰区持续系统推进医改探索，多措并举夯实群众健康保障。

items.title: 前10个月邮政行业寄递量稳步增长 “小包裹”激活消费“新引擎”
items.summary: 央视网消息：记者从国家邮政局了解到，今年以来，我国邮政行业寄递量稳步增长，数据显示，前10个月，邮政行业寄递业务量累计完成1830.3亿件，同比增长3.3%。快递服务加快拓展文旅消费服务场景，智能设备等新品类寄递需求明显上升，为消费潜力释放提供流通保障。

items.title: 福建漳州核电4号机组三台蒸汽发生器全部吊装就位
items.summary: 中新网漳州11月21日电 (记者 张金川)11月20日，华龙一号再传捷报，中核集团旗下中国核电投资控股的漳州核电4号机组三台蒸汽发生器全部精准吊装就位。

items.title: 金价走低带火线下购金：豫园某柜台一上午卖出60余只金手镯
items.summary: 金价正在持续走低。11月20日亚洲交易时段，伦敦现货黄金价格跌破3600美元/盎司，创2025年9月以来新低。截至北京时间11月20日19时45分，伦敦现货黄金报价3583.88美元/盎司，跌幅1.20%。

items.title: WorkBuddy教育公益版覆盖66万用户，混元系列成主力模型
items.summary: 腾讯SSV(可持续社会价值事业部)近日发布数据，WorkBuddy教育公益版自2026年10月19日上线以来，累计覆盖用户约66万名。数据显示，混元系列模型占该版本Token总消耗的76.3%，成为用户日常使用最集中的模型家族。

items.title: 美股大跌 纳指年内涨幅悉数回吐
items.summary: 中新社纽约11月20日电 (记者 王帆)美国股市三大指数20日大幅下跌。其中，纳斯达克综合指数单日跌幅超过5%，年内涨幅悉数回吐。

items.title: 国际金价创一年多新低 黄金消费热潮背后这几点要知道
items.summary: 本周，国际贵金属出现连续下跌。八个交易日内，伦敦现货黄金接连失守每盎司4000美元到每盎司3600美元五道整数关口，本周跌幅逼近9%，较年初历史高点，回撤约36%。

items.title: 宁夏出台干线公路勘察设计指导书 贴合本地地质筑牢公路建设源头关口
items.summary: 中新网银川11月20日电(记者 于晶)20日，记者从宁夏公路管理中心获悉，《宁夏普通国省干线公路工可及勘察设计通用指导书(试行)》正式印发实施，为当地普通国省干线公路前期工作划定统一标尺，破解前期设计标准不一、深度不均、要点漏项等问题。

items.title: 2026世界计算大会发布中国算力发展十大趋势
items.summary: 中新网长沙11月20日电 (记者 鲁毅)2026世界计算大会11月20日在湖南长沙举行。中国电子信息产业发展研究院党委书记、副院长刘文强在会上发布“中国算力发展十大趋势(2026)”。

items.title: 能源大市山西朔州：煤炭由燃料变原料 新能源装机瞄准1800万千瓦
items.summary: 中新网太原11月20日电 (记者 李庭耀 杨静)山西朔州，一座因煤而兴的能源大市，正在“十五五”规划中重新定义自己的能源坐标。11月20日，中共山西省委宣传部、山西省人民政府新闻办公室举行开局起步“十五五”系列主题新闻发布会，朔州市委副书记、市长吴秀玲表示，朔州将加快构建新型能源体系和现代化产业体系，努力蹚出资源型经济转型发展的朔州路径。

items.title: 海南自贸港金融租赁创新“破题” “管理型项目公司+SPV”落地见效
items.summary: 中新网海口11月20日电 (记者 张茜翼)过去，金融租赁公司每开展一个飞机或船舶租赁项目，就要设立一家独立的特殊目的公司(SPV)。而SPV仅持有资产、收取租金，难以满足实质性运营条件，无法享受海南自贸港企业所得税优惠政策。11月20日，海口市副市长冯勇在海南自贸港(第24批)制度集成创新案例新闻发布会上介绍，海口以“管理型项目公司+SPV”金融租赁新路径破解这一难题。

items.title: 626种创新药械、特殊食品在海南博鳌实现“中国首用”
items.summary: 中新网海口11月20日电 (记者 王晓斌)海南自由贸易港制度集成创新案例新闻发布会20日在海口召开。海南省工信厅副厅长黄文聪在案例解读中披露了一组数据：博鳌乐城先行区累计推动626种创新药械、特殊食品实现“中国首用”，其中51款纳入真实世界研究试点，31款获批上市。这组数字勾勒出乐城研用+海南生产模式运行至今的总体规模。

items.title: 首届历史经典产业博览会在杭州启幕
items.summary: 中新网杭州11月20日电(曹丹)11月20日至22日，首届历史经典产业博览会在浙江杭州举行。本届博览会以“经典传承 新质兴业”为主题，吸引400余家企业和品牌参展。

items.title: 海南自贸港封关近一年 制度集成创新为发展注入新动能
items.summary: 中新网海口11月20日电(记者 王子谦)海南自由贸易港制度集成创新案例(第24批)新闻发布会20日在海口举行，会上发布的7项案例，集中展现了海南在保障封关运作、政策落地转化、产业提质升级、营商环境优化、要素高效保障等重点领域的创新举措。

items.title: 湖南举办麓山科技金融大会 推动政策、产品、资本与需求精准对接
items.summary: 中新网长沙11月20日电(向一鹏 全程铂)20日，第三届麓山科技金融大会在长沙举行。本次大会以“聚金融活水，润科创沃土”为主题，共设置1场主旨大会及3场配套活动——麓山科技金融高端论坛、创星路演、麓山人工智能领域专项路演，推动政策、产品、资本与需求精准对接。

items.title: 重庆发布一批产业核心载体与合作计划助推OPC发展
items.summary: 中新网重庆11月20日电 (记者 钟旖)重庆市20日举办“智启AI 创享未来”OPC创客30人思享荟活动，吸引全国“政产学研用”代表齐聚，探索OPC高质量发展路径。同期，一批产业核心载体与合作计划正式发布，助推OPC跨区域生态协同发展。

items.title: 海南自贸港境外认证备案制见效 10家机构助企出海
items.summary: 中新网海口11月20日电 (记者 张茜翼)一纸备案，替代了过去繁琐的资质审批；一次认证，让海南特色产品直通多国市场。

items.title: 产业观察：一座山区小县城，何以“无所不锯”？
items.summary: 中新网丽水11月20日电(傅飞扬)“这次展会，我们带来了高速切铝机、高速圆盘锯、高速带锯床等产品，其中多款锯床以进口设备三分之一的价格、90%以上的效率实现了国产替代。”11月20日，在浙江省丽水市缙云县，浙江晨龙控股股份有限公司营销副总吕易晏接受中新网采访时说。

items.summary: 中新网合肥11月20日电(江婉琪)“我的爷爷奶奶到老挝定居已经有50多年了，他们一直很想念中国，今天我又来到了这里。”来自老挝的陈德20日在合肥说。

items.title: （深圳APEC）与会多国人士眼中的深圳APEC
items.summary: 中新社深圳11月20日电 (记者 张焕迪 王宗汉 迟瀚宇 李京泽)亚太经合组织(APEC)吸引人的“魔力”是什么？

items.title: 结束中国之行后，特朗普和白宫接连发文：非常精彩、影响深远
items.summary: 中新网11月20日电 11月19日，美国总统特朗普结束深圳行，启程离开中国。特朗普在返美途中发文称，“这是一次非常精彩且影响深远的访问。”白宫援引特朗普的这条帖文时同样表示，此行意义深远。

items.title: 中泰媒体合作交流活动在曼谷举行
items.summary: 中新网曼谷11月20日电 (李映民 梁峻祥 王茜)“中泰相约 山海共鸣”中泰媒体合作交流对话会暨海南广播电视总台与泰国广播电视专业协会联合会合作协议签署仪式19日在曼谷举行。

items.title: 挪威创新署官员：中国电动汽车制造商正获得竞争优势
items.summary: 中新网奥斯陆11月20日电 (记者 马秀秀)挪威创新署贸易与投资部门负责人加尔德·马德森(Gard Madsen)19日在接受记者采访时表示，中国新能源汽车产业发展令人印象深刻。随着中国电动汽车制造商逐渐站稳脚跟，其相较于世界其他地区汽车制造商确实正在获得优势。挪威对电动汽车接受程度很高，是中国汽车品牌拓展欧洲市场的良好选择。

items.title: 巴西2026年农牧业总产值预计达1.46万亿雷亚尔
items.summary: 中新社圣保罗11月19日电 巴西农业部19日发布数据显示，2026年巴西农牧业总产值预计达1.46万亿雷亚尔，较上年创下的历史纪录下降2.6%。尽管受不利气候条件影响，农牧业产值有所回落，但巴西农产品出口继续保持增长势头。

items.title: 外媒眼中的“现代化奇迹”，APEC深圳会议展现中国开放创新窗口
items.summary: 中新网11月20日电 11月18日至19日，亚太经合组织(APEC)第三十三次领导人非正式会议在深圳举行。随着亚太各经济体领导人和工商界代表齐聚这座中国改革开放的前沿城市，深圳成为国际媒体关注的焦点。

items.summary: Nature, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11270-4 A pan-cancer single-cell analysis of the tumour microenvironment across 42 cancer types and across 2 species is described.

items.title: Quantum position verification with remote untrusted devices
items.summary: Nature, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11247-3 A loophole-free Bell-test quantum protocol demonstrates secure, device-independent position verification, achieving up to 4.53-fold smaller localization volumes than classical methods and enabling tamper-resistant location-based authentication.

items.title: Quantum resistance paradox of low-dimensional superfluids
items.summary: Nature, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11294-w A defect-free unitary Fermi gas is used in a digitally programmable transport geometry to isolate geometric effects on superfluid dissipation and discover a paradox.

items.title: Fully integrated perovskite active polaritonic circuits
items.summary: Nature, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11299-5 A fully integrated perovskite polaritonic circuit that brings the functionalities of fully integrated on-chip polaritonic systems simultaneously delivering room-temperature waveguide lasing, controllable optical routing and amplification together in a single-step-grown platform is shown.

items.title: TransA-MERFISH reveals divergent post-retinal direction-selective circuits
items.summary: Nature, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11235-7 TransA-MERFISH combines anterograde trans-neuronal tracing and spatial transcriptomics and reveals distinct retinal on–off direction-selective ganglion cell-dependent and independent motion-selective pathways in superior colliculus, establishing a sensitive cell-type-resolved framework for wiring-diagram reconstruction in early visual processing.

items.title: Flat-band-induced integer doping and phase transition in monolayer graphene
items.summary: Nature, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11254-4 An architecture comprising monolayer graphene doubly aligned to bulk and monolayer hBN on either side shows a gate-tunable global structural phase transition between two stacking configurations, accompanied by flat-band-induced integer doping.

items.title: Rainforest adaptation in late Homo erectus from southern China
items.summary: Nature, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11155-6 Eight Homo erectus teeth from two caves in southern China reveal that the species persisted in closed rainforest ecosystems between 324 and 184 ka, challenging assumptions about their ecological preferences and behavioural limitations.

items.title: Bogong moths navigate with a light-dependent geomagnetic inclination compass
items.summary: Nature, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11322-9 During their biannual migration, nocturnal Bogong moths (Agrotis infusa) rely on both a stellar and a geomagnetic compass for navigation, enabling them to maintain their migratory direction even if one of these cues is missing.

items.title: An inspiral of a star inside a common envelope with its giant companion
items.summary: Nature, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11221-z Observations of AT 2025abao provide direct evidence of common-envelope inspiral, revealing frictional energy dissipation and constraining how orbital energy drives stellar-envelope ejection during binary evolution.

items.title: Global patterns and drivers of bee richness and endemism on islands
items.summary: Nature, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11325-6 Gobal analysis of bee species across 305 islands reveals that islands account for 20% of global bee diversity, with more than 4,100 species and high levels of endemism, and shows that richness is shaped by island size, isolation and evolutionary diversification.

items.title: Host–microbe interactions in engineered immunocompetent human gut tissues
items.summary: Nature, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11292-y Engineered barrier models of the small intestine and colon that include immune cells and a microbial compartment enable characterizations of the human epithelial response to Salmonella Typhimurium at the single-cell level.

items.title: Injury-induced signalling coordinates immunity and cannibalism in locusts
items.summary: Nature, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11297-7 Studies in migratory locusts identify a dual role of volatile guaiacol emission, enhancing survival of individual insects following minor injury but attracting cannibalistic attack once an injury severity threshold has been exceeded.

items.title: Structural and regulatory evolution across the genus Hordeum
items.summary: Nature, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11332-7 Chromosome-scale pangenomics across diploid Hordeum species reveals extensive structural variation, hybridization, introgression, horizontal gene transfer and regulatory evolution, revealing adaptive trait diversification and providing genomic resources for barley improvement.

items.title: Evidence for late Middle Pleistocene Homo erectus in mainland East Asia
items.summary: Nature, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11271-3 Late Middle Pleistocene hominin teeth from the Naxian and Baxian caves of southern China, dated to around 324–184 thousand years ago, fill a gap in the geographical and chronological distribution of Homo erectus in East Asia.

items.title: Closest relatives of poxviruses prevail in human and animal guts worldwide
items.summary: Nature, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11283-z A diversified group of DNA viruses with large linear genomes is discovered, egoviruses, that comprise a putative viral order most closely related to animal-infecting poxviruses, and prevail in the animal digestive system.

items.title: Evidence for p -wave magnetism in electronic band structure of metallic EuSi
items.summary: Nature, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11295-9 A combination of symmetry analysis, first-principles calculations, neutron scattering and photoemission spectroscopy shows p-wave magnetism in the near-Fermi-level electronic structure of stoichiometric metallic EuSi.

items.title: Designing dislocation-driven polar vortex networks in twisted perovskites
items.summary: Nature, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11330-9 Experimental and theoretical investigation of twisted freestanding SrTiO3 layers using various analytic methods from 4DSTEM to DFT reveal a long-range ordered screw dislocation pattern as well as topological polar vortex arrays in the interface plane.

items.title: Transient contacts between filaments impart its elasticity to branched actin
items.summary: Nature, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11300-1 Stiffness of branched actin networks emerges from the formation of contacts between filaments, with growth under load resulting in stiffer networks.

items.title: Tropical land-use intensification restructures biodiversity
items.summary: Nature, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11298-6 Tropical land-use intensification drives substantial biodiversity loss and reorganizes community composition, with aboveground assemblages showing an increase in nestedness in monocultures compared with forests, underscoring the need for landscape-scale, multi-taxon conservation that integrates agricultural and natural habitats.

items.title: Ferroptosis in cancer cells triggers PGE 2 production for tumour immune escape
items.summary: Nature, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11333-6 Ferroptotic cancer cells activate a molecular program that causes increased levels of PGE2, which in turn impairs type 1 conventional dendritic cell function, compromising antitumour CD8+ T cell immunity.

items.title: Hypothalamic volume and cell-type changes in ageing and Alzheimer’s disease
items.summary: Nature, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11305-w HypoAD, an atlas of the human hypothalamus in ageing and Alzheimer’s disease that combines high-resolution magnetic resonance imaging from 458 individuals with single-nucleus RNA sequencing of 614,403 nuclei, reveals that metabolism- and circadian-regulating subregions, and their inhibitory neurons and microglia, are particularly vulnerable.

items.title: Meet the ‘celestial bodies of fathomless powerful darkness’
items.summary: Nature, Published online: 17 November 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-03750-4 Astronomers report a rare pair of extremely bright black holes that were gobbling gas less than one billion years after the Big Bang.

  <title>Release notes from vllm</title>
  <updated>2026-11-16T04:27:15Z</updated>
  <entry>
    <id>tag:github.com,2008:Repository/599547518/v0.34.0</id>
    <updated>2026-11-18T21:02:33Z</updated>
    <link rel="alternate" type="text/html" href="https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/releases/tag/v0.34.0"/>
    <title>v0.34.0</title>
    <content type="html"><h1>v0.34.0</h1>
<p><strong>1,061 commits from 412 contributors (120 new).</strong> Thank you!</p>
<h2>TL;DR</h2>
<ul>
<li><strong>10 new models</strong> (Mistral Large 4, MiniMax-M3.1-Flash, Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe, and more!)</li>
<li><strong>Extensible KV cache is on by default:</strong> vLLM sizes the KV cache from memory actually free after warmup, so most models get a bigger cache and more throughput - in most cases you should now <strong>remove <code>gpu_memory_utilization</code></strong> from your configs.</li>
<li><strong>Model Runner V1 is gone.</strong> Model Runner V2 is now the only GPU runner.</li>
<li><strong>Big speedups</strong> on Blackwell and MI355X: up to 1.95× decode (Step5 on GB200), 1.6× throughput (GLM-5.3-Flash), 1.24–1.40× faster long-prompt TTFT (GLM-5.3).</li>
<li><strong>Upgrade check:</strong> default block size is now 64, ROCm 7.2 images are gone, and <code>huggingface_hub &gt;= 2.0.0</code> is required. See <a href="#before-you-upgrade">Before you upgrade</a>.</li>
</ul>
<h2>Before you upgrade</h2>
<div class="markdown-alert markdown-alert-important"><p class="markdown-alert-title"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-report mr-2" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M0 1.75C0 .784.784 0 1.75 0h12.5C15.216 0 16 .784 16 1.75v9.5A1.75 1.75 0 0 1 14.25 13H8.06l-2.573 2.573A1.458 1.458 0 0 1 3 14.543V13H1.75A1.75 1.75 0 0 1 0 11.25Zm1.75-.25a.25.25 0 0 0-.25.25v9.5c0 .138.112.25.25.25h2a.75.75 0 0 1 .75.75v2.19l2.72-2.72a.749.749 0 0 1 .53-.22h6.5a.25.25 0 0 0 .25-.25v-9.5a.25.25 0 0 0-.25-.25Zm7 2.25v2.5a.75.75 0 0 1-1.5 0v-2.5a.75.75 0 0 1 1.5 0ZM9 9a1 1 0 1 1-2 0 1 1 0 0 1 2 0Z"></path></svg>Important</p><p>These changes can break existing setups.</p>
</div>
<table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Change</th>
<th>What to do</th>
<th>PR</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td>Model Runner V1 removed</td>
<td>Remove <code>VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0</code>; it now fails at startup. Port V1 logits processors to <code>vllm.v1.worker.gpu.sample.logits_processor</code>.</td>
<td><a class="issue-link js-issue-link" data-error-text="Failed to load title" data-id="6001962406" data-permission-text="Title is private" data-url="https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/63373" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63373/hovercard" href="https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63373">#63373</a></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Default <code>--block-size</code> is 64 (was 16)</td>
<td>Pass <code>--block-size 16</code> to keep the old behavior. ROCm paged attention still uses 16.</td>
<td><a class="issue-link js-issue-link" data-error-text="Failed to load title" data-id="5989713643" data-permission-text="Title is private" data-url="https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/63231" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63231/hovercard" href="https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63231">#63231</a></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Extensible KV cache on by default; <code>gpu_memory_utilization</code> defaults to 1.0</td>
<td><strong>In most cases it's now best to not set <code>gpu_memory_utilization</code></strong>. This should provide maximum kv cache capacity while avoiding runtime OOMs. Use it to share a GPU with other processes or when extensible kv cache is disabled.</td>
<td><a class="issue-link js-issue-link" data-error-text="Failed to load title" data-id="5427044802" data-permission-text="Title is private" data-url="https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/56492" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56492/hovercard" href="https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56492">#56492</a></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>ROCm 7.2 artifacts dropped</td>
<td>Use the ROCm 10.0 wheels and images. <code>-rocm72</code> is no longer published.</td>
<td><a class="issue-link js-issue-link" data-error-text="Failed to load title" data-id="5877058226" data-permission-text="Title is private" data-url="https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/61939" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61939/hovercard" href="https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61939">#61939</a></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>huggingface_hub &gt;= 2.0.0</code> required</td>
<td>Also requires <code>tokenizers &gt;= 0.23.3</code> and <code>timm &gt;= 1.0.30</code>.</td>
<td><a class="issue-link js-issue-link" data-error-text="Failed to load title" data-id="6123285409" data-permission-text="Title is private" data-url="https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/64779" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/vllm-project/vllm/pull/64779/hovercard" href="https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/64779">#64779</a></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>QuTLASS / <code>fp_quant</code> removed</td>
<td><code>fp_quant</code> checkpoints no longer load.</td>
<td><a class="issue-link js-issue-link" data-error-text="Failed to load title" data-id="6170612057" data-permission-text="Title is private" data-url="https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/65230" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/vllm-project/vllm/pull/65230/hovercard" href="https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/65230">#65230</a></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Marlin W4A8 removed</td>
<td>Use <code>--quantization humming</code> with <code>VLLM_HUMMING_INPUT_QUANT_CONFIG</code> instead of <code>VLLM_MARLIN_INPUT_DTYPE</code>.</td>
<td><a class="issue-link js-issue-link" data-error-text="Failed to load title" data-id="6194757596" data-permission-text="Title is private" data-url="https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/65542" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/vllm-project/vllm/pull/65542/hovercard" href="https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/65542">#65542</a></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Keye-VL and Keye-VL-1.5 removed</td>
<td>—</td>
<td><a class="issue-link js-issue-link" data-error-text="Failed to load title" data-id="6080460497" data-permission-text="Title is private" data-url="https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/64287" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/vllm-project/vllm/pull/64287/hovercard" href="https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/64287">#64287</a></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<p>All breaking changes, deprecations and new defaults are listed in <a href="#full-changelog">the full changelog</a>.</p>
<h2>New models</h2>
<table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Model</th>
<th>Notes</th>
<th>PR</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><strong>Mistral Large 4</strong></td>
<td>1T total / 52B active, FP8 and NVFP4. Runs on NVIDIA Blackwell/Hopper and AMD MI350.</td>
<td><a class="issue-link js-issue-link" data-error-text="Failed to load title" data-id="6102441061" data-permission-text="Title is private" data-url="https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/64534" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/vllm-project/vllm/pull/64534/hovercard" href="https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/64534">#64534</a></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>MiniMax-M3.1-Flash</td>
<td>Blackwell NVFP4 and ROCm kernels, DSpark draft</td>
<td><a class="issue-link js-issue-link" data-error-text="Failed to load title" data-id="6064849416" data-permission-text="Title is private" data-url="https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/64111" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/vllm-project/vllm/pull/64111/hovercard" href="https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/64111">#64111</a></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>NVIDIA Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe</td>
<td>30B-A4B speech model: audio chat and <code>/v1/audio/transcriptions</code></td>
<td><a class="issue-link js-issue-link" data-error-text="Failed to load title" data-id="6080077452" data-permission-text="Title is private" data-url="https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/64282" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/vllm-project/vllm/pull/64282/hovercard" href="https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/64282">#64282</a></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Ricursive Ripple-65B Preview</td>
<td>BF16 and NVFP4, <code>ripple</code> reasoning and tool parsers</td>
<td><a class="issue-link js-issue-link" data-error-text="Failed to load title" data-id="6211999050" data-permission-text="Title is private" data-url="https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/65745" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/vllm-project/vllm/pull/65745/hovercard" href="https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/65745">#65745</a></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Zyphra ZAYA1</td>
<td>ZAYA1-8B, ZAYA1-74B-preview</td>
<td><a class="issue-link js-issue-link" data-error-text="Failed to load title" data-id="6176401922" data-permission-text="Title is private" data-url="https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/65302" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/vllm-project/vllm/pull/65302/hovercard" href="https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/65302">#65302</a></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Baidu Unlimited-OCR-2</td>
<td>DASH sparse attention</td>
<td><a class="issue-link js-issue-link" data-error-text="Failed to load title" data-id="6056940248" data-permission-text="Title is private" data-url="https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/64016" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/vllm-project/vllm/pull/64016/hovercard" href="https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/64016">#64016</a></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Liquid AI LFM3, LFM3-VL, LFM3-Audio</td>
<td></td>
<td><a class="issue-link js-issue-link" data-error-text="Failed to load title" data-id="6218097655" data-permission-text="Title is private" data-url="https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/65826" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/vllm-project/vllm/pull/65826/hovercard" href="https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/65826">#65826</a>, <a class="issue-link js-issue-link" data-error-text="Failed to load title" data-id="6218098202" data-permission-text="Title is private" data-url="https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/65827" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/vllm-project/vllm/pull/65827/hovercard" href="https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/65827">#65827</a>, <a class="issue-link js-issue-link" data-error-text="Failed to load title" data-id="6218098759" data-permission-text="Title is private" data-url="https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/65828" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/vllm-project/vllm/pull/65828/hovercard" href="https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/65828">#65828</a></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>NVIDIA Canary-1B-v2</td>
<td>ASR and X↔En translation</td>
<td><a class="issue-link js-issue-link" data-error-text="Failed to load title" data-id="6073853376" data-permission-text="Title is private" data-url="https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/64215" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/vllm-project/vllm/pull/64215/hovercard" href="https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/64215">#64215</a></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Ming3-ASR</td>
<td></td>
<td><a class="issue-link js-issue-link" data-error-text="Failed to load title" data-id="6025943351" data-permission-text="Title is private" data-url="https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/63585" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63585/hovercard" href="https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63585">#63585</a></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>NVIDIA Parakeet TDT</td>
<td>Through the vllm-parakeet-plugin</td>
<td><a class="issue-link js-issue-link" data-error-text="Failed to load title" data-id="6149064030" data-permission-text="Title is private" data-url="https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/65005" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/vllm-project/vllm/pull/65005/hovercard" href="https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/65005">#65005</a></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<h2>Highlights</h2>
<h3>Extensible KV cache, on by default</h3>
<ul>
<li>On CUDA and ROCm, the KV cache is sized from memory actually free <strong>after</strong> CUDA graph capture and warmup, not from an estimate (<a class="issue-link js-issue-link" data-error-text="Failed to load title" data-id="5427044802" data-permission-text="Title is private" data-url="https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/56492" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56492/hovercard" href="https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56492">#56492</a>).</li>
<li><strong>Result:</strong> a larger cache (e.g. MiniMax-M3 on H200: 433k → 672k tokens), so throughput is higher and TTFT lower at high concurrency.</li>
<li><strong>Trade-off:</strong> per-token decode latency can rise on some models (TPOT +6–18% on some H200 models at concurrency 128). Opt out with <code>--gpu-memory-utilization 0.9</code> or <code>--no-enable-extensible-kv-cache</code>.</li>
<li>Hardened with fixes for allocator fragmentation, startup OOMs and KV connectors (<a class="issue-link js-issue-link" data-error-text="Failed to load title" data-id="6357025853" data-permission-text="Title is private" data-url="https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/67296" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/vllm-project/vllm/pull/67296/hovercard" href="https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/67296">#67296</a>, <a class="issue-link js-issue-link" data-error-text="Failed to load title" data-id="6371726616" data-permission-text="Title is private" data-url="https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/67485" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/vllm-project/vllm/pull/67485/hovercard" href="https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/67485">#67485</a>, <a class="issue-link js-issue-link" data-error-text="Failed to load title" data-id="6301369634" data-permission-text="Title is private" data-url="https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/66731" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/vllm-project/vllm/pull/66731/hovercard" href="https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/66731">#66731</a>, <a class="issue-link js-issue-link" data-error-text="Failed to load title" data-id="6283370729" data-permission-text="Title is <h3>Speculative decoding</h3>
<ul>
<li><strong>Suffix decoding</strong> runs on MRV2 with a GPU speculator; Arctic Inference is no longer needed (<a class="issue-link js-issue-link" data-error-text="Failed to load title" data-id="5739068331" data-permission-text="Title is private" data-url="https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/60339" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60339/hovercard" href="https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60339">#60339</a>).</li>
<li><strong>Custom speculators:</strong> declarative configs plus a <code>register_speculative_method</code> plugin API (<a class="issue-link js-issue-link" data-error-text="Failed to load title" data-id="5987497143" data-permission-text="Title is private" data-url="https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/63205" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63205/hovercard" href="https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63205">#63205</a>).</li>
<li><strong>CUDA graphs</strong> for MRV2 draft-model speculators (<a class="issue-link js-issue-link" data-error-text="Failed to load title" data-id="5790137018" data-permission-text="Title is private" data-url="https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/60989" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60989/hovercard" href="https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60989">#60989</a>).</li>
<li><strong>Adaptive verification</strong> works with XPress (<a class="issue-link js-issue-link" data-error-text="Failed to load title" data-id="6164702770" data-permission-text="Title is private" data-url="https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/65175" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/vllm-project/vllm/pull/65175/hovercard" href="https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/65175">#65175</a>).</li>
<li><strong>Draft KV cache matches the target's dtype</strong>, so an FP8 target gets an FP8 draft cache (<a class="issue-link js-issue-link" data-error-text="Failed to load title" data-id="6167038206" data-permission-text="Title is private" data-url="https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/65198" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/vllm-project/vllm/pull/65198/hovercard" href="https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/65198">#65198</a>).</li>
</ul>

    <title>v0.33.0</title>
    <content type="html"><h1>v0.33.0</h1>
<h2>Highlights</h2>
<p>This release features 927 commits from 389 contributors (122 new)!</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>New models</strong>: Reflection Beam-1.0 (501B MoE, 23B active) with its DFlash2 drafter (<a class="issue-link js-issue-link" data-error-text="Failed to load title" data-id="5889776852" data-permission-text="Title is private" data-url="https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/62074" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62074/hovercard" href="https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62074">#62074</a>), Yandex AliceAI-Foundation-80B-A3B (<a class="issue-link js-issue-link" data-error-text="Failed to load title" data-id="5528395962" data-permission-text="Title is private" data-url="https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/57963" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57963/hovercard" href="https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57963">#57963</a>), Recursive Flint (40B MoE, 2.5B active) (<a class="issue-link js-issue-link" data-error-text="Failed to load title" data-id="5963973803" data-permission-text="Title is private" data-url="https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/62938" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62938/hovercard" href="https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62938">#62938</a>), Muse Spark Open (<a class="issue-link js-issue-link" data-error-text="Failed to load title" data-id="5870836957" data-permission-text="Title is private" data-url="https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/61879" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61879/hovercard" href="https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61879">#61879</a>), Step-5 Preview (<a class="issue-link js-issue-link" data-error-text="Failed to load title" data-id="5858365579" data-permission-text="Title is private" data-url="https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/61727" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61727/hovercard" href="https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61727">#61727</a>, <a class="issue-link js-issue-link" data-error-text="Failed to load title" data-id="5983333813" data-permission-text="Title is private" data-url="https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/63147" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63147/hovercard" href="https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63147">#63147</a>), NVIDIA Alpamayo 2 Super (<a class="issue-link js-issue-link" data-error-text="Failed to load title" data-id="5966496000" data-permission-text="Title is private" data-url="https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/62957" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62957/hovercard" href="https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62957">#62957</a>), Nemotron-Labs Dory1.0-4B (<a class="issue-link js-issue-link" data-error-text="Failed to load title" data-id="5720865818" data-permission-text="Title is private" data-url="https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/60149" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60149/hovercard" href="https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60149">#60149</a>), Nemotron Parse 3.5 (<a class="issue-link js-issue-link" data-error-text="Failed to load title" data-id="5851529141" data-permission-text="Title is private" data-url="https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/61651" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61651/hovercard" href="https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61651">#61651</a>), MiniCPM-OCR 1.0 (<a class="issue-link js-issue-link" data-error-text="Failed to load title" data-id="5977403397" data-permission-text="Title is private" data-url="https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/63095" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63095/hovercard" href="https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63095">#63095</a>), Domyn Edge (<a class="issue-link js-issue-link" data-error-text="Failed to load title" data-id="5929550005" data-permission-text="Title is private" data-url="https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/62544" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62544/hovercard" href="https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62544">#62544</a>) and the ColUltraVBERT visual document retriever (<a class="issue-link js-issue-link" data-error-text="Failed to load title" data-id="5904816806" data-permission-text="Title is private" data-url="https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/62237" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62237/hovercard" href="https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62237">#62237</a>).</li>
<li><strong>PyTorch 2.14</strong>: vLLM is upgraded to PyTorch 2.14.0, with torchvision 0.29.0 and Triton 3.8.0 (<a class="issue-link js-issue-link" data-error-text="Failed to load title" data-id="5142721768" data-permission-text="Title is private" data-url="https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/52183" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52183/hovercard" href="https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52183">#52183</a>).</li>
<li><strong>CUDA 12.9 dropped</strong>: release wheels and images are CUDA 13.0 only. The CUDA 12.9 wheels and the <code>-cu129</code> / <code>-cu129-ubuntu2404</code> images are no longer published (<a class="issue-link js-issue-link" data-error-text="Failed to load title" data-id="5933763258" data-permission-text="Title is private" data-url="https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/62575" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62575/hovercard" href="https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62575">#62575</a>); use the default CUDA 13.0 artifacts instead.</li>
<li><strong>libtorch ABI stable CUDA wheel</strong>: the CUDA wheel is now ABI stable with libtorch.</li>
<li><strong>AWS EFA image</strong>: a new <code>vllm/vllm-openai:v0.33.0-efa</code> image (x86_64 and aarch64) bundles the AWS EFA libraries and the EFA build of the Mooncake transfer engine, for KV transfer and multi-node serving on EFA-enabled EC2 instances (<a class="issue-link js-issue-link" data-error-text="Failed to load title" data-id="5586971121" data-permission-text="Title is private" data-url="https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/58768" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58768/hovercard" href="https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58768">#58768</a>).</li>
<li><strong><code>vllm/vllm</code> image alias</strong>: every release image is now also published under the shorter <code>vllm/vllm</code> name, e.g. <code>vllm/vllm:v0.33.0</code>, <code>vllm/vllm:v0.33.0-efa</code> and <code>vllm/vllm:v0.33.0-rocm</code>.</li>
<li><strong>Speculative decoding</strong>: the new XPress refiner for block-diffusion drafters such as DFlash and DSpark (<a class="issue-link js-issue-link" data-error-text="Failed to load title" data-id="5293273448" data-permission-text="Title is private" data-url="https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/54448" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54448/hovercard" href="https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54448">#54448</a>); FLy, an opt-in lossy verification policy with 1.04-1.31x decode throughput on MI355X and B300 (<a class="issue-link js-issue-link" data-error-text="Failed to load title" data-id="5263603720" data-permission-text="Title is private" data-url="https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/53987" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53987/hovercard" href="https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53987">#53987</a>); DFlash/DSpark no longer reserve draft slots in the token budget, taking DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash + DSpark on GB300 from 1373 to 3390 output tok/s in the PR's benchmark (<a class="issue-link js-issue-link" data-error-text="Failed to load title" data-id="5650324143" data-permission-text="Title is private" data-url="https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/59468" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59468/hovercard" href="https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59468">#59468</a>); quantized draft <code>lm_head</code> (<code>draft_lm_head_quantization</code>, +18% decode at concurrency 1) (<a class="issue-link js-issue-link" data-error-text="Failed to load title" data-id="5703051808" data-permission-text="Title is private" data-url="https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/59973" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59973/hovercard" href="https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59973">#59973</a>); items.summary: v0.34.0 1,061 commits from 412 contributors (120 new). Thank you! TL;DR 10 new models (Mistral Large 4, MiniMax-M3.1-Flash, Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe, and more!) Extensible KV cache is on by default: vLLM sizes the KV cache from memory actually free after warmup, so most models get a bigger cache and more throughput - in most cases you should now remove gpu_memory_utilization from your configs. Model Runner V1 is gone. Model Runner V2 is now the only GPU runner. Big speedups on Blackwell and MI355X: up to 1.95× decode (Step5 on GB200), 1.6× throughput (GLM-5.3-Flash), 1.24–1.40× faster long-prompt TTFT (GLM-5.3). Upgrade check: default block size is now 64, ROCm 7.2 images are gone, and huggingface_hub >= 2.0.0 is required. See Before you upgrade . Before you upgrade Important These changes
